evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% and 5% 1,2-pentylene glycol (vehicle not specified), single patient patch test
evidence.support_text: Positive skin sensitization reactions were observed in a patient patch tested with 0.5% and 5% 1,2-pentylene glycol, while the control group showed no reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% and 5% aqueous pentylene glycol; patient with facial dermatitis
evidence.support_text: A 68-year-old, nonatopic female developed facial dermatitis after using an eye cream that contained pentylene glycol (1,2-pentanediol), and patch test results were positive. Positive patch test reactions (+1) to 0.5% and 5% aqueous pentylene glycol were also reported.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% and/or 1% ortho-phenylphenol (OPP) solution; patch test read within 72 h
evidence.support_text: Three cases of dermatitis were described in connection with the use of OPP in a medical hand cream and/or a coolant. Patch tests with 0.5% and/or 1% OPP solution were positive within 72 h (Adams, 1981; Van Hecke, 1986).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% DEP in 99% ethanol or cream base; occluded patch test for 24–48 h; 231 patients (mostly with contact dermatitis)
evidence.support_text: A 24–48-h occluded patch test was conducted using 0.5% DEP in 99% ethanol or in a cream base. Of 231 patients, four showed marked erythema and two showed slight erythema (Takenaka et al., 1986).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% in petrolatum, Finn chamber, readings at D2 and D3 according to ICDRG criteria
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old female with eyelid dermatitis was patch tested; the only positive patch test was coconut diethanolamide (0.5% pet.) ++ at D2 and D3; after removal of the shampoo containing this allergen, the dermatitis cleared.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% in petrolatum, readings at day 2 and day 3
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old female with eyelid dermatitis had a positive patch test (++) to coconut diethanolamide (0.5% pet.) at D2 and D3, and the dermatitis cleared upon removal of the allergen from shampoo.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% in petrolatum, readings at day 2 and day 3, Finn chamber
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old female with eyelid dermatitis was patch tested with standard and additional series; the only positive patch test was coconut diethanolamide (0.5% pet.) with ++ reactions at D2 and D3, leading to a diagnosis of allergic contact dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.5% in petrolatum; readings at D2 and D3; female patient with eyelid dermatitis
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old non-atopic female with eyelid dermatitis had a positive patch test to coconut diethanolamide 0.5% pet. (++ at D2 and D3). After removing the shampoo containing this allergen, the dermatitis cleared.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.81% o-Cresol; 10 hand dermatitis patients
evidence.support_text: Out of 10 hand dermatitis patients, no effects were observed at 0.81% o-Cresol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% and 5% nimesulide in white soft paraffin, occlusive patch, readings at 48 h and 96 h
evidence.support_text: Six months after initial presentation, the patient was patch tested with nimesulide 1% and 5% in white soft paraffin. The 5% preparation produced an erythematous reaction at 48 h that became papular at 96 h. A less florid erythematous reaction to the 1% preparation was evident at 48 h and persisted at 96 h. Patch tests to both preparations in 20 healthy controls were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aq. juglone, 2-day occlusion with Finn Chambers and Scanpor tape, readings at D2, D3, D4, D7
evidence.support_text: Patch tests were performed with juglone (1% aq.) using standard technique. Only the hydroalcoholic extract of walnut husk elicited a bullous irritant reaction on D2, indicating that juglone itself did not elicit an allergic contact dermatitis reaction in this patient.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aqueous CAPB patch test; patients with eczematous eruptions of scalp and/or hand dermatitis
evidence.support_text: Another 6 patients referred for eczematous eruptions of the scalp and/or hand dermatitis had positive 1% aqueous CAPB patch test reactions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aqueous CAPB, patch tested as part of standard series from January 1995 to September 1998
evidence.support_text: Armstrong et al. patch tested patients with suspected contact dermatitis from January 1995 to September 1998 using 1% aqueous CAPB; of the 10,798 patients tested, 29 (0.27%) had a positive reaction to CAPB, and 23 of the 29 cases were deemed relevant with dermatitis on the face, neck, hands, or widespread areas.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aqueous CAPB; second group of 102 patients suspected of cosmetic dermatitis; patch tested with cosmetic screening series
evidence.support_text: In a second group of 102 patients suspected of cosmetic dermatitis patch tested with 1% aqueous CAPB, only 3 patients (3%) had a positive reaction; they had been using products containing CAPB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% aqueous soap solution, patch test read on D4
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with 1% aqueous solutions of both laundry bar soap brands resulted in a ++ positive reaction on D4. The patient's erythema multiforme-like lesions were confined to contact areas with the soap.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% Carvacrol, patch test on contact dermatitis patients
evidence.support_text: One of two contact dermatitis patients patch tested with 1% Carvacrol elicited a positive response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% formulation in different vehicles; tested on dermatitis patients
evidence.support_text: Large-scale studies on dermatitis patients (altogether more than 16,000) where OPP has been patch tested (among other substances) mostly as a 1% formulation in different vehicles revealed allergic reactions in less than 0.4% in each case and also some irritative reactions (Brasch et al., 1993; Geier et al., 1996; Goh et al., 1994; Grattan et al., 1989; Schnuch et al., 1998; Storrs et al., 1989; Uter et al., 1993).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% in water, patch test, patients with suspected contact dermatitis, Netherlands, 1985
evidence.support_text: In a 1985 multicentre study from The Netherlands, 501 patients were patch tested with 1% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water, resulting in a 0.6% positive reaction rate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% nicotine salicylate in routine patch tests on 312 patients with dermatitis
evidence.support_text: In 312 routine patch tests on patients with dermatitis, 17 showed weak and 2 showed strong reactions to 1% nicotine salicylate (Swineford and Radford).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% nimesulide in white soft paraffin, patch test, readings at 48 h and 96 h
evidence.support_text: The patient was patch tested to nimesulide using 1% and 5% preparations in white soft paraffin. The 1% preparation resulted in an erythematous reaction at 48 h that persisted at 96 h. Patch tests to both preparations in 20 healthy controls were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% Thymol in petrolatum; 48-h closed patch test
evidence.support_text: A 43-year-old man with chronic paronychia on the big left toe developed spreading pruritic dermatitis after applying Listerine under occlusion. A 48-h closed patch test with 1% Thymol in petrolatum gave a +2 reaction in the patient and no reaction in 3 controls (Fisher 1989).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% xylene, patch test reading at 15 minutes
evidence.support_text: Altman described a case of allergic contact urticaria presenting as facial dermatitis. Patch testing showed a 15-mm urticarial patch to 1% xylene at 15 minutes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1.5% ethylhexyl dimethyl PABA in white Vaseline applied to humans
evidence.support_text: No skin sensitization was observed in humans following application of 1.5% ethylhexyl dimethyl PABA mixed with white Vaseline.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Ethyl Methacrylate; 48-hour occlusive patch; reading at 96 hours
evidence.support_text: Condé-Salazar, Guimaraens, and Romero (1988) patch-tested six workers with dermatitis from anaerobic sealants; five of the workers had positive reactions to 10% Ethyl Methacrylate after 96 hours.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Urea cream, 48 h patch test
evidence.support_text: A 10% Urea cream was patch tested in 79 patients with eczematous skin disease for 48 h. Positive patch test reactions were observed in 7 out of 79 patients (9.9%), indicating skin sensitization. The overall report notes there are few reports of sensitization among many clinical studies using Urea on diseased skin.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Urea cream, occlusive 48-h patch test on patients with eczematous skin disease
evidence.support_text: Cramers and Thormann (1981) tested 79 patients with eczematous skin disease with a cream that contained 10% Urea under occlusion as a 48-h patch test. Positive patch test reactions were observed in 7/79 patients (9.9%) and another 5 had erythematous reactions on the 5th day after treatment.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% Urea cream, occlusive 48-h patch test, reaction observed on day 5
evidence.support_text: Another 5 patients had erythematous reactions on the 5th day after treatment with the 10% Urea cream under occlusion.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 100% xylene, patch test reading at 15 minutes
evidence.support_text: Altman described a case of allergic contact urticaria presenting as facial dermatitis. Patch testing showed an immediate 25-mm urticarial patch to 100% xylene at 15 minutes.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 102 healthy male and female participants, same procedure as reference 89
evidence.support_text: An eye makeup remover containing 20% isohexadecane was tested in 102 participants according to the same procedure and showed no evidence of skin irritation or sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 104 healthy male and female participants
evidence.support_text: An eye shadow containing 47.64% isododecane was tested in 104 healthy participants and results were negative for skin irritation and sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 108 participants during induction, 100 during challenge, 2 cm × 2 cm patch
evidence.support_text: An eyeliner containing 40.16% isododecane was tested (2 cm × 2 cm patch) on 108 participants during induction and 100 during challenge; results were negative for skin irritation and sensitization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 109 cases of rubber dermatitis; patch test with MBT
evidence.support_text: Wilson (ref4) reported that in 109 cases of rubber dermatitis, patch tests with MBT showed a positive rate of 47%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 109 cases of rubber dermatitis; patch test with PTD
evidence.support_text: Wilson (ref4) reported that in 109 cases of rubber dermatitis, patch tests with dipentamethylenethiuramdisulfide (PTD) showed a positive rate of 68%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 109 cases of rubber dermatitis; patch test with TMTD
evidence.support_text: Wilson (ref4) reported that in 109 cases of rubber dermatitis, patch tests with TMTD showed a positive rate of 54%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 109 cases of rubber dermatitis; patch test with zinc diethyldithiocarbamate (ZDC)
evidence.support_text: Wilson (ref4) reported that in 109 cases of rubber dermatitis, patch tests with zinc diethyldithiocarbamate (ZDC) showed a positive rate of 24%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 11 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with MBT
evidence.support_text: Brand (ref7) reported that in 11 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with MBT were positive in 10 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 11 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with TMTD
evidence.support_text: Brand (ref7) reported that in 11 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with TMTD were positive in 5 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 13 eligible employees patch tested
evidence.support_text: None of the other employees who agreed to be patch tested had positive reactions to Coating C, Chemical Y, or polyvinyl butyral; however, some employees with severe dermatitis did not participate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% citral; vehicle not reported; cosmetic dermatitis patients (1978–1986)
evidence.support_text: Patch tests with 2% citral (vehicle not reported) conducted between 1978–1986 in cosmetic dermatitis patients showed reactions in 1/240 patients (Itoh et al., 1986, 1988; Nishimura et al., 1984).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% citral; vehicle not reported; non-cosmetic dermatitis patients (1978–1986)
evidence.support_text: Patch tests with 2% citral (vehicle not reported) conducted between 1978–1986 in non-cosmetic dermatitis patients showed reactions in 2/584 patients (Itoh et al., 1986, 1988; Nishimura et al., 1984).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% in water, patch test, patients with suspected contact dermatitis, Denmark, 1976-1977
evidence.support_text: A multicentre Danish study from 1976–1977 patch tested 694 patients with 2% tris(N-hydroxyethyl)hexahydrotriazine in water and reported a 2% positive reaction rate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2% TDI solution; patch tested on 26 TDI-exposed workers reporting skin symptoms
evidence.support_text: In a flexible foam plant, 26 TDI exposed workers reporting skin symptoms underwent patch testing with a 2% TDI solution, but none developed a reaction to the TDI antigen.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2-day occlusive application on upper back, reading on day 3, European standard series and plastics/glues series (Chemotechnique)
evidence.support_text: Positive reactions were observed with PBO (o-Phenylenediamineterephthalonitrile, D3+++) in patch testing on the upper back using the European standard series and a series of plastics and glues, indicating that the patient developed skin sensitization to PBO.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 20 g/100 mL aqueous patch, 48 hours, Piperazine-K preparation
evidence.support_text: In Table I (p. 33–34), aqueous patches of Piperazine-K at 20 g/100 mL were applied for 48 hours to 6 men including the sensitized subject J.M. All subjects showed nil reaction (score 0), indicating no skin irritation or allergic response under these conditions.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 220 female patients suspected of cosmetic-related contact dermatitis; patch tested with 1% and 5% kojic acid in petrolatum or similar vehicle; reactions read as + and ++
evidence.support_text: Of the 220 female patients patch tested for suspected cosmetic-related contact dermatitis, 5 reacted to kojic acid as well as products they owned that contained 1% kojic acid. Reactions to 1% and 5% kojic acid in these patients were + and ++. The remaining 215 patients in the patch test group did not have any reactions to kojic acid.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 23 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with DDG
evidence.support_text: Saito and Yamakashiki (ref5) reported that in 23 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with DDG were positive in 7 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 23 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with MBT
evidence.support_text: Saito and Yamakashiki (ref5) reported that in 23 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with MBT were positive in 9 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 23 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with tetramethylthiuram monosulfide (TS)
evidence.support_text: Saito and Yamakashiki (ref5) reported that in 23 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with tetramethylthiuram monosulfide (TS) were positive in 5 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 23 rubber dermatitis patients; patch test with TMTD
evidence.support_text: Saito and Yamakashiki (ref5) reported that in 23 rubber dermatitis patients, patch tests with TMTD were positive in 4 cases.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 24-h and 72-h readings; 19-year-old female patient with dermatitis on hands, forearms, and face
evidence.support_text: A 19-year-old female gardener with dermatitis of the hands, forearms and face after frequent contact with different cultivars of common ivy was patch tested with didehydrofalcarinol. The latter was negative at the 24-h reading but gave a ++ reaction after 72 h, indicating a positive patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Clemmensen (1984) GPMT; day 0: intradermal injection of 10% Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate in neck; day 7: 250 mg 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate in petrolatum for 24h; day 8: topical induction with 100% Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate under patch for 48h; day 21: challenge with 25% Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate; scores read at 48 and 72h.
evidence.support_text: Clemmensen (1984) performed a GPMT inducing guinea pigs with Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate. Animals induced with Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate had positive cross-reactions when challenged with 25% Hydroxypropyl Methacrylate (3 of 12).

evidence.experimental_conditions: bixin 10–40 µM, HaCaT cells, non-cytotoxic conditions (MTT and annexinV-PI confirmed)
evidence.support_text: Using a dual luciferase ARE-reporter assay in immortalized human HaCaT keratinocytes, dose-dependent induction of NRF2 transcriptional activity was elicited by bixin treatment at concentrations (10–40 µM) devoid of cytotoxicity as detected by MTT assay and annexinV-PI staining.

evidence.experimental_conditions: primary mouse keratinocytes from Nrf2-/- mice; 4-HNE treatment; HO-1 mRNA measurement
evidence.support_text: In keratinocytes from Nrf2-/- mice, 4-HNE was significantly less effective in upregulating HO-1 mRNA expression compared to wild type keratinocytes, indicating that Nrf2 mediates the response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Normal human keratinocytes (NHK), 10-20 µM resveratrol, 16 h incubation, fluorescence microscopy with anti-Nrf2 antibodies, HCS quantification.
evidence.support_text: Normal human keratinocytes exposed to 10-20 µM resveratrol for 16 h showed a 30% increase in nuclear Nrf2 fluorescence measured by high-content screening, while cytoplasmic Nrf2 was not significantly changed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: bixin 20 µM, 24 h, primary human epidermal keratinocytes (HEKs)
evidence.support_text: Immunoblot analysis confirmed NRF2 activation in HEKs in response to bixin treatment as evident from increased protein levels of NRF2 and NRF2 targets including NQO1, AKR1C2, HO-1, TrxR, GCLM, SRXN1, and FTH1 (Fig. 1B, 20 µM, 24 h; Fig. 1D, time course with bixin 20 µM).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 24-hour treatment with MMF (concentration not specified in the provided text)
evidence.support_text: Monometryl fumarate (MMF) induced a significant increase in both total and nuclear Nrf2 levels in primary mouse keratinocytes, as determined by immunofluorescence.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Primary mouse keratinocytes; 500 µM, 750 µM, or 1 mM MMF; 16 h; anti-Nrf2 antibody and Cy3-conjugated secondary; ImageJ quantification
evidence.support_text: MMF treatment (500 µM, 750 µM, 1 mM) for 16 hours resulted in a dose-dependent increase in nuclear Nrf2 levels in keratinocytes, as assessed by immunofluorescence. Nuclear Nrf2 levels were significantly greater than control at all tested concentrations.

evidence.experimental_conditions: UV-PAPC 100 µg/ml, 2 h treatment, primary human keratinocytes, immunofluorescence microscopy
evidence.support_text: Immunofluorescence microscopy showed increased nuclear accumulation of NRF2 in cultured human keratinocytes 2 h after stimulation with UV-PAPC (100 µg/ml) as shown in Supplemental Fig. 1.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Nrf2+/+ mice; bixin 200 mg/kg i.p. 48 h before solar UV exposure; skin collected 24 h post-UV; IHC analysis
evidence.support_text: In Nrf2+/+ mice, bixin (200 mg/kg i.p.) dramatically induced the cutaneous NRF2 pathway, detectable by immunohistochemistry for NRF2, GCLM, and AKR1C1 proteins.

evidence.assay_type: in vitro Nrf2 pathway activation in HaCaT keratinocytes
evidence.experimental_conditions: Human HaCaT keratinocyte cell line; likely standard culture conditions
evidence.support_text: PdNP were shown to activate the Nrf2 pathway in keratinocytes in vitro (Goldstein et al. 2016).

evidence.experimental_conditions: HaCaT human keratinocyte cell line; human skin organ culture model
evidence.support_text: The abstract states that nitroxides may act as electrophiles, directly or indirectly, capable of activating the Keap1–Nrf2–ARE pathway in human keratinocytes (HaCaT) and in human skin (human organ culture model).

evidence.experimental_conditions: BALB/c and CBA/J mice; vehicle: AOO; dose range: 10, 25, 50% for both strains
evidence.support_text: In the LLNA: BrdU-FCM study with BALB/c and CBA/J mice, Cinnamic alcohol (CA) was classified as a skin sensitizer in both mouse strains.

evidence.support_text: In the LLNA: BrdU-FCM study with BALB/c and CBA/J mice, 2-Mercaptobenzothiazole (MBT) was evaluated as a non-sensitizer in both mouse strains.

evidence.support_text: In the LLNA: BrdU-FCM study with BALB/c and CBA/J mice, Salicylic acid (SA) was evaluated as a non-sensitizer in both mouse strains.

evidence.support_text: For CMI/MI, LLNA: BrdU-FCM with BALB/c gave an EC2.7 of 1.062% (category Moderate).

evidence.support_text: Mixtures of oligo(2-(2-ethoxy)ethoxyethyl) guanidinium chloride (PGH) with propylene glycol (PG) at ratios of 9:1, 4:1, and 1:4 (w/w) were all positive in terms of skin sensitization potential in the LLNA: BrdU-FCM assay.

evidence.support_text: According to the OECD TG 442B guidelines, the LLNA: BrdU-FCM predicts that a substance is positive for SS if its SI is ≥2.7. PG had SI values lower than 2.7 at all test concentrations (25%, 50%, 100%) and thus was predicted to be negative (nonsensitizer).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Application to murine epidermal cells, 4h post application; RT-PCR with liquid hybridization
evidence.support_text: IL-10 mRNA signals were uniformly enhanced 4h after application of TNCB to murine epidermal cells, as assessed by RT-PCR with liquid hybridization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Application to murine epidermal cells, RT-PCR with liquid hybridization (time not specified)
evidence.support_text: Experiments with an irritant (SLS) demonstrated that only contact allergens enhanced IL-10 mRNA signals; the irritant did not enhance signals, as measured by RT-PCR with liquid hybridization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Application to murine epidermal cells, RT-PCR with liquid hybridization (time not specified)
evidence.support_text: Experiments with tolerogens including DNTB demonstrated that only contact allergens enhanced IL-10 mRNA signals; tolerogens did not enhance signals, as measured by RT-PCR with liquid hybridization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Application to murine epidermal cells, RT-PCR with liquid hybridization (time not specified, but likely 4h as in TNCB experiments)
evidence.support_text: Experiments with other contact sensitizers including DNCB demonstrated that only contact allergens enhanced IL-10 mRNA signals, as measured by RT-PCR with liquid hybridization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Application to murine epidermal cells, RT-PCR with liquid hybridization (time not specified, but likely 4h as in TNCB experiments)
evidence.support_text: Experiments with other contact sensitizers including DNFB demonstrated that only contact allergens enhanced IL-10 mRNA signals, as measured by RT-PCR with liquid hybridization.

evidence.experimental_conditions: rats, administration of HQ (route unspecified), tissue analysis
evidence.support_text: Covalent adducts of HQ to protein sulfur nucleophiles were detected in rat tissues following administration of HQ. The concentration of total adducts was greatest in the liver, followed by kidney and blood, with tissue-specific patterns of mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-substituted adducts.

evidence.experimental_conditions: mass spectrometry, synthesis confirmation
evidence.support_text: A thioether could be isolated and identified with mass spectrometry from rats treated with 2-chloroBMN. The structure was confirmed by synthesis and appeared to be N-acetyl-S-[2-chlorobenzyl]-L-cysteine (2-chlorobenzylmercapturic acid).
